title: Select flat polynomial parameters in a regular closed fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\Lambda$ a Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $q\subset\Lambda$ prime. Put $L=\Lambda_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Fix $t,r\ge0$, $x_j\in\Lambda$ for $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(t)$ and $y_i\in q$ for $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ with the $y_i/1$ generating $qL$. Put $\varphi_0:k[X_j]\to\Lambda$, $X_j\mapsto x_j$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $p_0=\varphi_0^{-1}(q)$ and $I_0=p_0L$. Assume the canonical map $k[X_j]_{p_0}\to L$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $L/I_0$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then there are $e\ge0$ and $s:\operatorname{Fin}(e)\to\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ such that, for $\varphi:k[X_j,Y_i]\to\Lambda$ sending $X_j$ to $x_j$ and $Y_i$ to $y_{s(i)}$, the canonical map $k[X_j,Y_i]_{\varphi^{-1}(q)}\to L$ is flat and $qL=I_0+(y_{s(i)}/1\mid i\in\operatorname{Fin}(e))$.

proof.text: Put L=Λ_q and let I₀ be the first contracted polynomial prime extended to L. The quotient S=L/I₀ is regular local. Images of ys generate its maximal ideal, so their cotangent images span. Select a basis from this finite spanning family, with indices s:Fin e→Fin r. Nakayama makes these lifts generators; their number is the embedding dimension, equal to the Krull dimension, so they are regular parameters and a regular sequence. Lift generation to m_L=I₀+(ys(s_i)/1).

Define the appended polynomial map using Fin.addCases, and its localization A₁ at the contracted prime. The maps A₀→A₁→L are local and all three rings are Noetherian. The closed fibre of A₀→A₁ is κ(p₀)[Y_i] localized at the origin: all Y_i belong to the prime and their ideal is already maximal over the residue field. Its localization is regular local of dimension e with parameters Y_i.

The closed-fibre map sends Y_i to the selected regular sequence in S, whose final quotient is nonzero. The regular-parameter criterion 07DY gives fibre flatness. Apply 00MP with base A₀, middle A₁, target L and finite nonzero L-module L, using hflat for flatness over A₀. This gives flatness over A₁. The resulting map is the canonical localRingHom by uniqueness of localization. If S is a field, select e=0; the argument also covers r=0.

theorem exists_flat_regular_fibre_parameter_selection
    (k : Type u) (Λ : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime]
    (t r : ℕ) (xs : Fin t → Λ) (ys : Fin r → Λ)
    (hyq : ∀ i, ys i ∈ q)
    (hys : Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (ys i))) =
      q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)))
    (hflat : (Localization.localRingHom
      (q.comap (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) xs).toRingHom) q
      (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) xs).toRingHom rfl).Flat)
    (hfibre : IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
      (q.comap (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) xs).toRingHom).map
        ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp
          (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) xs).toRingHom))) :
    ∃ (e : ℕ) (s : Fin e → Fin r),
      let φ : MvPolynomial (Fin (t + e)) k →ₐ[k] Λ :=
        MvPolynomial.aeval (Fin.addCases xs (fun i ↦ ys (s i)))
      (Localization.localRingHom (q.comap φ.toRingHom) q φ.toRingHom rfl).Flat ∧
        q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) =
          (q.comap (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) xs).toRingHom).map
              ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp
                (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) xs).toRingHom) ⊔
            Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦
              algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (ys (s i))))
